job_statement: When I need to enable Pipelines as Code for my source repository, I want to create a Repository CR that matches events from my Git repository, so I can automate pipeline runs triggered by repository events.
prerequisites: Have namespace created for pipeline runs
Have access to create CRs in the target namespace
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to enable automated pipeline runs
Ensure events from repository are correctly matched
Reduce likelihood of pipeline runs executing in wrong namespace
evidence: using-repository-crd-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Creating the Repository custom resource (module: op-creating-repository-cr.adoc), lines 76-104. Key content: 'You can use the tkn pac CLI or other alternative methods to create a Repository custom resource (CR) inside the target namespace... Whenever an event comes from a URL such as https://github.com/<repository>/<project>, {pac} matches it and checks out the repository content.'
notes: Main job covering Repository CR creation. Multiple approaches possible (tkn pac CLI or other methods). Includes important security constraint about namespace targeting.

job_statement: As a Platform Engineer, when I need to create a Repository CR, I want to use the tkn pac CLI or kubectl to define the repository URL and namespace, so I can quickly connect my Git repository to Pipelines as Code.
parent_job: Create a Repository CR that matches events from my Git repository
prerequisites: Have kubectl or tkn pac CLI installed
Have target namespace created
desired_outcomes: Complete Repository CR creation in under 5 minutes
Avoid syntax errors in CR definition
evidence: using-repository-crd-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Creating the Repository custom resource (module: op-creating-repository-cr.adoc), lines 80-96. Shows example: 'cat <<EOF|kubectl create -n my-pipeline-ci -f-' with Repository CR spec including url field.
notes: User story showing CLI-based approach to creating Repository CR. Example shows kubectl but mentions tkn pac as alternative.

job_statement: When multiple Repository CRs could match the same Git repository event, I want to use explicit namespace targeting annotations, so I can prevent unauthorized pipeline runs in namespaces where I don't have access.
parent_job: Create a Repository CR that matches events from my Git repository
prerequisites: Understand Repository CR matching behavior
Have Repository CR created
desired_outcomes: Eliminate risk of malicious actors executing pipelines in unauthorized namespaces
Ensure only intended namespace processes repository events
evidence: using-repository-crd-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Creating the Repository custom resource (module: op-creating-repository-cr.adoc), lines 98-103. States: 'If many Repository CRs match the same event, {pac} processes only the oldest one. If you need to match a specific namespace, add the pipelinesascode.tekton.dev/target-namespace annotation. Such explicit targeting prevents a malicious actor from executing a pipeline run in a namespace to which they do not have access.'
notes: Security-focused user story addressing namespace isolation. Important for multi-tenant scenarios.

section: Creating the global Repository custom resource
job_statement: When I manage multiple repositories with common settings, I want to create a global Repository CR with shared configuration, so I can avoid repeating the same settings across multiple repository-specific CRs.
prerequisites: Have administrator access to openshift-pipelines namespace
Have common settings identified (secrets, git provider config)
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to configure new repositories
Reduce likelihood of configuration inconsistencies across repositories
Ensure centralized management of common settings
evidence: using-repository-crd-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Creating the global Repository custom resource (module: op-creating-global-repository-cr.adoc), lines 113-164. States: 'Optionally, you can create a global Repository custom resource (CR) in the namespace where you installed {pipelines-shortname}, normally openshift-pipelines. If you create this CR, the settings that you specify in it apply by default to all Repository CRs that you create.' Example shows gitlab-webhook-config secrets shared across all repositories.
notes: Technology Preview feature. Main job for centralized configuration management across multiple repositories.

section: Creating the global Repository custom resource

Have Git provider secrets created

desired_outcomes: Complete global configuration in single operation
Ensure all repository CRs inherit common settings automatically

job_statement: When I need to control resource usage for pipeline runs, I want to set concurrency limits on a Repository CR, so I can prevent too many pipeline runs from executing simultaneously and overwhelming cluster resources.
prerequisites: Have Repository CR created
Understand resource capacity of cluster
desired_outcomes: Minimize risk of resource exhaustion from concurrent pipeline runs
Ensure predictable pipeline run execution order
Reduce likelihood of pipeline failures due to resource contention
evidence: using-repository-crd-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Setting concurrency limits (module: op-setting-concurrency-limits-in-repository-crd.adoc), lines 173-196. States: 'You can use the concurrency_limit spec in the Repository custom resource definition (CRD) to define the maximum number of pipeline runs running simultaneously for a repository.' Example shows concurrency_limit field with behavior: 'If there are many pipeline runs matching an event, the pipeline runs that match the event start in an alphabetical order.'
notes: Main job for controlling pipeline run concurrency. Important for resource management and preventing cluster overload.

job_statement: As a Platform Engineer, when multiple pipeline runs match a single event, I want to set concurrency_limit in the Repository CR spec, so I can ensure only a specified number run simultaneously while others queue in alphabetical order.
parent_job: Set concurrency limits on a Repository CR
prerequisites: Have Repository CR created
Have multiple pipeline runs defined in .tekton directory
desired_outcomes: Complete concurrency configuration by adding single field
Ensure deterministic execution order for queued pipeline runs
evidence: using-repository-crd-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Setting concurrency limits (module: op-setting-concurrency-limits-in-repository-crd.adoc), lines 179-196. Shows spec example with 'concurrency_limit: <number>' field. Explains: 'if you have three pipeline runs in the .tekton directory and you create a pull request with a concurrency_limit of 1, then {pac} executes all the pipeline runs in alphabetical order. At any given time, only one pipeline run is in the running state. The system queues the rest.'
notes: User story showing YAML configuration approach. Alphabetical ordering provides deterministic behavior.

section: Changing the source branch for the pipeline definition
job_statement: When I need to enforce pipeline definition review before execution, I want to configure the Repository CR to fetch pipeline definitions from the default branch, so I can ensure all pipeline changes are reviewed and merged before they can execute.
prerequisites: Have Repository CR created
Have default branch defined in Git repository
Have merge review process established
related_jobs: Review and merge pipeline definition changes
desired_outcomes: Eliminate risk of unreviewed pipeline definitions executing
Ensure pipeline changes undergo merge review process
Minimize likelihood of malicious pipeline runs from untrusted pull requests
evidence: using-repository-crd-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Changing the source branch for the pipeline definition (module: op-changing-source-branch-in-repository-crd.adoc), lines 205-229. States: 'By default, {pac} fetches the pipeline definition from the branch that triggered the event. To fetch the definition from the default branch instead (such as main, master, or trunk), set pipelinerun_provenance in the Repository custom resource definition (CRD).' Note explains: 'Use this setting as a security precaution... you must merge the pipeline definition into the default branch before {pac} runs it. This ensures that merge reviews verify all changes.'
notes: Main job focused on security through enforced review process. Important security control for preventing malicious pipeline runs.

section: Changing the source branch for the pipeline definition
job_statement: As a Platform Engineer, when I want to prevent unreviewed pipeline definitions from executing, I want to set pipelinerun_provenance to default_branch in the Repository CR settings, so I can force all pipelines to use reviewed definitions from the default branch.
parent_job: Configure the Repository CR to fetch pipeline definitions from the default branch
prerequisites: Have Repository CR created
Have default branch protection configured
related_jobs: Merge pipeline definition changes to default branch
desired_outcomes: Complete security configuration by setting single field
Ensure 100% of pipeline runs use reviewed definitions
evidence: using-repository-crd-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Changing the source branch for the pipeline definition (module: op-changing-source-branch-in-repository-crd.adoc), lines 211-223. Shows YAML example with 'settings: pipelinerun_provenance: default_branch' configuration. Note states this is 'a security precaution' ensuring 'merge reviews verify all changes.'
notes: User story showing configuration approach for security control. Prevents pipeline definition injection via pull requests.

job_statement: When I need to manage pipeline parameters centrally without modifying pipeline runs in Git, I want to define custom parameters in the Repository CR, so I can control values like registry URLs or account identifiers from the Repository CR location.
prerequisites: Have Repository CR created
Have pipeline runs using custom parameters
Understand difference between Tekton parameters and custom parameters
related_jobs: Define pipeline runs with parameter placeholders
Manage parameter values in Repository CR
desired_outcomes: Minimize need to modify pipeline runs in Git for environment-specific values
Ensure centralized control of administrator-managed parameters
Reduce likelihood of hardcoded environment-specific values in pipeline definitions
evidence: using-repository-crd-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Custom parameter expansion (module: op-custom-parameter-expansion.adoc), lines 237-306. States: 'You can use {pac} to expand a custom parameter within your PipelineRun resource by using the params field. You can specify a value for the custom parameter inside the template of the Repository custom resource (CR). The specified value replaces the custom parameter in your pipeline run.' Use cases include: 'To define a URL parameter, such as a registry URL that varies based on a push or a pull request. To define a parameter, such as an account UUID that an administrator can manage without necessitating changes to the PipelineRun execution in the Git repository.'
notes: Main job for centralized parameter management. Note warns this is complementary to Tekton parameters, not a replacement. Custom parameters enable admin-controlled values separate from developer-controlled pipeline definitions.

job_statement: As a Platform Engineer, when I need to provide environment-specific values to pipeline runs, I want to define custom parameters in the Repository CR params field with static values or secret references, so I can inject administrator-managed values without changing pipeline definitions in Git.
parent_job: Define custom parameters in the Repository CR
prerequisites: Have Repository CR created
Have pipeline runs referencing custom parameters
Have secrets created if using secret_ref
related_jobs: Create Kubernetes secrets for parameter values
desired_outcomes: Complete parameter configuration without modifying Git repository
Ensure parameter values are injected into all matching pipeline runs
Minimize time to update parameter values across all pipeline runs
evidence: using-repository-crd-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Custom parameter expansion (module: op-custom-parameter-expansion.adoc), lines 254-280. Shows two examples: static value approach 'params: - name: company value: ABC Company' and secret reference approach 'params: - name: company secret_ref: name: my-secret key: companyname'. States: 'The value ABC Company replaces the parameter name company in your pipeline run and in the remotely fetched tasks.'
notes: User story showing two implementation approaches: direct values and secret references. Values replace parameters in both pipeline runs and remote tasks.

job_statement: When I need different parameter values for different event types, I want to define multiple custom parameters with the same name but different CEL filters, so I can provide different values for push events versus pull request events.
parent_job: Define custom parameters in the Repository CR
prerequisites: Have Repository CR created
Understand Common Expression Language (CEL) filter syntax
Have pipeline runs that need event-specific parameter values
related_jobs: Configure event filtering in pipeline runs
desired_outcomes: Ensure correct parameter values are used for each event type
Minimize complexity of parameter management across event types
Reduce likelihood of using wrong parameter value for event type
evidence: using-repository-crd-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Custom parameter expansion (module: op-custom-parameter-expansion.adoc), lines 288-304. Shows example with CEL filter: 'params: - name: company value: ABC Company filter: pac.event_type == pull_request'. Note states: 'When you have many parameters with the same name and different filters, {pac} uses the first parameter that matches the filter. You can then expand parameters according to different event types. For example, you can combine a push and a pull request event.'
notes: Advanced user story showing conditional parameter expansion based on event type. Uses CEL filters for matching logic. First matching parameter wins.
